## AEGIS has a front door now.

Run it and you get a menu: install the recommended stack, tune runtimes by
family or version, or open the Workbench on its own. AEGIS shows the plan
before it changes anything, then keeps you posted while each package installs.

This release also makes WinGet's own update path match how AEGIS is meant to
work: the newest prerelease is welcome, unless stable is ahead. If preview
lookup or installation goes sideways, AEGIS falls back to stable. Both release
files are checked against Microsoft's published SHA-256 hashes before use.

### What's in the box

- A keyboard-friendly menu, a clearer plan, and a readable end-of-run summary
- Runtime families you can select together or open up by version
- Workbench apps kept separate from the recommended gaming stack
- Corretto 21, 17, and 8 and .NET Framework 3.5 available when you need them
- Per-package progress, timings, useful failure details, and a log you can open
- WinGet prerelease support with stable fallback

Grab the versioned BAT for a quick start, or the ZIP or `tar.gz` for the full
folder. The compressed PowerShell script is there if that's what you prefer.
Checksums are included so you can verify the downloads. Bring your games; AEGIS
will bring the runtimes.
